title: Hassan Tower, Rabat
summary: The Hassan Tower is the unfinished minaret of the Hassan Mosque in Rabat, Morocco, begun under the Almohad ruler Yaqub al-Mansur. UNESCO dates the mosque's start to 1184, while History Hit gives about 1195. Work stopped when he died in 1199, and the tower stands 44 m high.

uncertainty.note: UNESCO says the Hassan Mosque was begun in 1184; History Hit says about 1195; the Museum With No Frontiers dates work to al-Mansur's reign (AD 1184-99) and says it halted at his death.

phases.description: Built under Yaqub al-Mansur (reigned 1184-99); UNESCO says the mosque was begun in 1184, History Hit about 1195.
Construction was halted at the monarch's death and the minaret left unfinished.
Shock waves of the 1755 Lisbon earthquake decapitated the minaret, now 44 m high.

reviewer_note: Shape tower, square (no diameter sourced). The base width rests on the French page only; the English page of the same publisher says 6.20 m, which cannot fit a 44 m tower, so treat 16.20 m as likely but unconfirmed by an independent page (an Archnet page was blocked). Start date conflicts: 1184 (UNESCO) versus about 1195 (History Hit). Phase 1199-1755 state altered is my label for the unfinished tower.
